messages:
ana (Support): customer reports intermittent 400 from /v1/rerank when sending batches of 4+ embeddings. They only see it in prod, dev is fine. sample req id: r-0a9f3c2e. payload shape looks ok on first glance (array of items each with 'query' + 'candidates' arrays) but dims sometimes reported as 1537 vs expected 1536 in the logs. attaching log excerpt below.

ana (Support): log snippet: ```
2026-01-18T15:32:10Z ERROR handler.cpp:237 request_id=r-0a9f3c2e RerankError: embedding dim mismatch: got 1537 expected 1536
2026-01-18T15:32:10Z DEBUG http: headers: {"content-encoding": "gzip", "content-type": "application/json"}
```

devon (ML Eng): thanks. can you paste the curl you used? also what model/version are they hitting (e.g., text-embed-ada-002 / v3)?

ana (Support): here's the curl they used (sanitized): ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \
  --data-binary @batch.json
```
attached batch.json (trimmed): ```json
{"queries":[{"id":"q1","text":"foo"}],"candidates":[["c1","c2","c3","c4"]],"embeddings":[[...1536 floats...],[...1536 floats...],[...1536 floats...],[...1536 floats...]]}
```

jen (Eng-ML): intermittent + off-by-one dim smells like a serialization boundary—maybe gzip write adds an extra byte when batching multiple arrays? do we see any corruption in the incoming bytes on the gateway? can we get raw request bytes for r-0a9f3c2e?

mike (Platform): I pulled the proxy logs for that request id. the Content-Length matches, but I see the proxy decompressed and forwarded as chunked. proxy log: ```
PROXY r-0a9f3c2e upstream-decompress ok chunked-forwarding
```

liv (Eng-SRE): tagging. @devon @jen can you request a debug-bundle from the customer (curl + base64 of gzip file) and enable raw-body capture for the next 30m for their org? I'll open a short-lived capture rule.

support-bot: Ticket #CS-8241 created for r-0a9f3c2e. SLA: P2.

devon (ML Eng): suggested repro steps for customer: 1) reproduce with --no-compress (remove Content-Encoding header) to confirm gzip path. 2) if still repros, send us the raw body: `cat batch.json | gzip -c | base64` and paste output. 3) include curl --trace-ascii to capture wire.

ana (Support): customer tried no-compress: they said the error disappeared when removing gzip header and sending raw JSON. they attached base64 payload (pasted into ticket).

jen (Eng-ML): ok that points to gzip handling. initial theory: our decompressor path incorrectly counts a trailing null or leftover buffer as another float when parsing embedded numeric arrays. can we repro locally by feeding the base64 into our ingest pipeline?

mike (Platform): repro locally: I decoded the base64, gunzipped and fed to our parsing util. parsing shows an extra comma at the end of the last vector in some batches (likely due to streaming chunk boundary join). quick diff: expected tail of vector `...,0.123]` vs observed `...,0.123,]` leading parser to treat as empty token -> interpreted as 0 or extra value.

liv (Eng-SRE): good find. can we get a minimal curl for them to test a fix client-side? maybe we should ask them to ensure gzip is produced with --no-name / deterministic output, or avoid streaming gz in this path until we patch.

devon (ML Eng): short-term mitigation: ask customers to remove Content-Encoding: gzip or ensure their gzip uses a single-shot file (not streaming) when batching embeddings. long-term: i'll add stricter validation on parse (reject trailing commas) and better tolerant parsing that errors before handing to embed loader.

ana (Support): sent customer instructions, included this repro test: ```
# reproduce server-side fix test
cat batch.json | gzip -c > batch.gz
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' --data-binary @batch.gz --trace-ascii debug.txt
```

devon (ML Eng): I'll open an internal backend ticket to add explicit gzip sanity check + better error message referencing request_id. putting in eng-ml board.

jen (Eng-ML): follow-up: add small unit test that simulates chunked gz streams with edge-case boundary to ensure parser rejects corrupted streams.

mike (Platform): rollout plan: patch parser in canary env first, keep old behavior with feature-flag off for 24h, then flip if no regressions. I'll coordinate with eng-oncall for deploy windows.

ana (Support): customer confirmed workaround (removed gzip) and resumed successful calls. closing loop and will update ticket CS-8241 with root cause and mitigation notes. :white_check_mark:
